ads_ratio.reason: EDGAR share counts are ordinary (A+B) shares and the Nasdaq price is per ADS; at a 1:1 ratio per-share figures are directly comparable to the ADS price with no scaling.
ads_ratio.source: Ericsson Form 20-F for FY2025 (filed 2026-03-12), cover page: 'American Depositary Shares (each representing one B share)'; the FY2025 annual report states the same: 'Each ADS represents one Class B share.'

moat_against: RAN is a re-bid, price-competitive product business — carriers squeeze vendors and no end user is locked in
Global RAN market flat between cycles; growth is hostage to carrier capex timing (India rollouts, North America digestion)
Huawei remains the global share leader and price aggressor outside restricted markets
IPR licensing income is lumpy and settlement-driven; margins exposed to component (memory) cost inflation not immediately passable to customers
Enterprise/Vonage capital allocation destroyed value — SEK 32B (2023) and SEK 15.1B (2024) impairments
moat_for: One of two Western RAN suppliers (with Nokia); EU/US high-risk-vendor phase-outs structurally exclude Huawei/ZTE from much of its market
Deep installed base with the world's largest carriers plus multi-year managed-services/software contracts — real switching friction in live networks
Top-tier cellular SEP portfolio generating a high-margin IPR licensing annuity
Scale R&D and standards leadership in 5G/early 6G that smaller vendors cannot match
moat_justification: One of only two Western RAN vendors with a top-tier cellular patent portfolio, deep carrier installed base and scale R&D — but RAN is a re-bid, capex-cycle product business with no end-customer lock-in, Huawei leads globally on price, the market is flat between 5G/6G cycles, and the Vonage excursion (SEK 32B + SEK 15.1B impairments) showed capital allocation can destroy the moat's earnings.
name: Telefonaktiebolaget LM Ericsson
one_liner: Western RAN duopolist with a top-tier patent annuity, net cash and a first-ever SEK 15B buyback, moat 5/10 — but a flat capex-cycle market, lumpy IPR and H2 2026 component-cost pressure leave weighted IRR at 12.6% (IV@15% $7.75 vs $9.58 price); Tier C — clears 15% only at ~$7.75 or below.

sbc_override.reason: The engine accepts a single override value applied to every unfilled period; SEK 1,790M is both the filed FY2025 expense and the median of the three filed gap-year figures (1,206 / 2,080 / 1,790), so the median-of-3-FY base is built from filed figures with offsetting errors of ~1% of OE in the non-median years. It is ~7.0x the last engine-filed value (FY2019 SEK 256M) — inside the 0.1x-10x band — and the step-up is real: the Key Contributor cash-settled plans scaled up from 2022 (Note G3). ~90% of the expense is cash-settled plans (a real cash cost through provisions); only SEK 175M of FY2025's total is share-settled.
sbc_override.source: Ericsson Form 20-F for FY2025 (filed 2026-03-12), Financial Report Note G3 'Share-based compensation', table 'Compensation expense for LTV 2022-2025': total compensation expense SEK 1,206M (2023), SEK 2,080M (2024), SEK 1,790M (2025). The engine's ifrs-full tag ExpenseFromSharebasedPaymentTransactionsWithEmployees is filed only through FY2019 (SEK 256M), so EDGAR companyfacts carries no SBC for 2020-2025.
